# Validate inputs
    arrs = [np.asarray(x) for x in [logp_with_result, logp_call_only, logp_no_call]]
    for arr in arrs:
        if arr.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError("Input must be 2D")
        if arr.size == 0:
            raise ValueError("Input cannot be empty")
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(arr)):
            raise ValueError("Input contains nonfinite values")
        if np.any(arr > 0):
            raise ValueError("Input contains positive values")
    shapes = [arr.shape for arr in arrs]
    if not all(s == shapes[0] for s in shapes):
        raise ValueError("Input shapes must match")
    n_candidates, future_horizon = shapes[0]

    if isinstance(tau_filter, bool):
        raise ValueError("Boolean threshold is invalid")
    if not np.isfinite(tau_filter):
        raise ValueError("Threshold must be finite")
    if tau_filter < 0:
        raise ValueError("Threshold must be nonnegative")

    # Compute normalized decreasing future-token weights
    t = np.arange(future_horizon, dtype=float)
    raw_weights = np.maximum(0, 1 - 0.2 * t)
    normalized_weights = raw_weights / raw_weights.sum()

    # Compute weighted future-token loss (negative weighted log probability)
    def compute_loss(logp):
        return -np.sum(logp * normalized_weights, axis=1)

    loss_empty = compute_loss(arrs[2])
    loss_call_only = compute_loss(arrs[1])
    loss_with_result = compute_loss(arrs[0])

    # Use stronger counterfactual baseline
    L_minus = np.minimum(loss_empty, loss_call_only)
    margin = L_minus - loss_with_result

    # Keep calls meeting the filtering threshold
    keep_mask = margin >= tau_filter

    return keep_mask, margin
